US-119-HR10947.title: Monitor Microplastics Now Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10947.description: To direct the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to include certain nanoplastics and microplastics on a certain list of unregulated contaminants published pursuant to the Safe Drinking Water Act, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10947.aiSummary: The bill would require the Environmental Protection Agency to add certain nanoplastics and microplastics to a drinking water list of unregulated contaminants. These are tiny plastic pieces smaller than 1,000 nanometers or 5 millimeters, and they would be added to the sixth version of that list. If that list has already been issued, the agency would have to issue it again with these substances included.

US-119-HR10925.title: Countering Online Trafficking Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10925.description: To require an assessment with respect to the technical capacity of the Department of State to address the use of artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to facilitate trafficking in persons.
US-119-HR10925.aiSummary: The bill would require the State Department to assess its technical ability to deal with the use of artificial intelligence and other new technology to help trafficking in people, especially trafficking involving children. It would also ask what staff or training gaps exist and what steps the department would take to fix them if needed. The report would be due within 180 days after the bill becomes law and would go to House and Senate foreign affairs committees.

US-119-HR10903.description: To direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to seek to enter into a lease for the purpose of establishing a Vet Center in Socorro, New Mexico, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10903.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Department of Veterans Affairs to try to lease space for a Vet Center in Socorro, New Mexico. The lease would need to start no later than December 31, 2027. It would affect veterans in the Socorro area who may use the center.

US-119-S5687.title: Presidential Pardon Integrity Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary under authority of the order of the Senate of 09/30/2026.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5687.description: A bill to codify the process for petitions for executive clemency, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5687.aiSummary: The bill would set rules for how people ask the President for pardons, commutations, reprieves, or fine relief. It would keep an Office of the Pardon Attorney in the Justice Department, spell out how petitions are reviewed, and require notice to some victims. It would also make people who receive clemency report certain information, and it would require public posting of some clemency details.

US-119-HR10826.title: Justice for Citizens Wrongfully Detained by ICE Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10826.description: To establish a private right of action for citizens of the United States who are arrested or detained by immigration officers or law enforcement officers enforcing the immigration laws without a warrant or probable cause, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10826.aiSummary: The bill would let U.S. citizens sue immigration officers or other law enforcement officers who enforce immigration laws if they are arrested or detained without a warrant or probable cause on or after January 20, 2025. If they win, the court would award $500,000 plus $100,000 for each day of detention, along with lawyer fees and other court-ordered relief. It also would end some unused immigration enforcement funds.

US-119-HR10804.title: Utility Accountability Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10804.description: To establish penalties for the failure of investor-owned electric utilities to meet State performance targets.
US-119-HR10804.aiSummary: The bill would set penalties for investor-owned electric utilities that do not meet state performance standards. If a utility fails to meet those standards, it would have to give residential customers a bill credit starting at $100 a year, with the amount increasing by $100 each year until the utility complies. If a state regulator does not follow the order, the Energy Secretary could withhold grants, loans, loan guarantees, and technical help from that state agency.

US-119-HR10749.title: RAISE Act of 2026
US-119-HR10749.summary:
Restore Agricultural Investment, Stability, and Expansion Act of 2026 or the RAISE Act of 2026

This bill allows the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to provide payments to producers of high-value crops (including citrus) for revenue losses or losses of crop quality or production that are a consequence of specific events. These events include a drought, wildfire, hurricane, flood, tornado, winter storm, and smoke exposure. USDA may implement this program by providing block grants to states and territories.

US-119-HR10749.aiSummary: The bill would let the Agriculture Department make payments to growers of high-value crops, including citrus, for lost income or lower crop quality or output after events like drought, wildfire, hurricanes, floods, tornadoes, winter storms, or smoke exposure. It would affect farmers who grow these crops. The department could also use block grants to states and territories to run the program.

US-119-S2398.title: Kay Hagan Tick Reauthorization Act
US-119-S2398.summary:
Kay Hagan Tick Reauthorization Act

This act reauthorizes through FY2030 activities of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to address vector-borne diseases (e.g., diseases spread by bites from ticks or mosquitoes). These activities include (1) a national strategy, (2) grants for regional centers of excellence, and (3) cooperative agreements with state, local, and tribal health departments to increase capacity for preventing and responding to vector-borne diseases.

US-119-HR10507.aiSummary: The bill would direct the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress by December 31, 2028, on expanding a terrorism-related legal rule so more people could seek payments when a terrorist attack caused injury but not death. It would look at how many more people could qualify, how much extra money would be needed, and what law changes would best make that happen, including for psychiatric injuries. US-119-HR6207.title: Chip EQUIP Act
US-119-HR6207.summary:
Chip Equipment Quality, Usefulness, and Integrity Protection Act of 2025 or the Chip EQUIP Act

This bill prohibits companies that receive certain federal funds from purchasing specified semiconductor manufacturing equipment made by foreign entities of concern (e.g., companies owned or controlled by China, Iran, North Korea, or Russia) or their subsidiaries for the federally funded project.

The CHIPS Act of 2022, which became law in August 2022, appropriated funding for the Department of Commerce to carry out the CHIPS for America provisions enacted in the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021. These provisions included appropriations for financial incentives to expand domestic manufacturing capacities across the semiconductor supply chain, as well as for research and development programs.

Under the bill, Commerce must include in the terms of each agreement with a covered entity (e.g., companies receiving CHIPS funds) prohibitions with respect to a project relating to the procurement, installation, or use of the specified semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The prohibitions must be effective for 10 years beginning on the date on which the agreement is signed.

The bill authorizes Commerce to waive these prohibitions under certain circumstances, such as if the specified semiconductor manufacturing equipment is not produced in the United States or an allied or partner country in sufficient and reasonably available quantities or of a satisfactory quality to support established or expected production capabilities.

US-119-HR1653.title: Civil Investigative Demand Reform Act of 2025
US-119-HR1653.summary:
Civil Investigative Demand Reform Act of 2025

This bill revises the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s (CFPB’s) civil investigative demand process. The demand process is used to gather information relevant to a violation of consumer financial law before formal proceedings.

Under the bill, such demands must be issued and served no later than six years after the date of the violation. The demand must also provide specific reference to particular facts regarding the violation.

The bill establishes a process that allows an advising attorney to submit questions on behalf of a person compelled by a demand to appear for oral testimony.

The bill also allows for judicial review if the CFPB denies a petition to set aside or modify a demand. These petitions must be treated as confidential.

In addition, the bill expands the grounds on which a petitioner may seek relief from such a demand to include a demonstration that the demand (1) is unduly burdensome, expensive, and outside the scope of the inquiry; (2) is unreasonably cumulative or duplicative; or (3) can be obtained from some other source that is more convenient, less burdensome, or less expensive.
US-119-HR1653.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in House, 2025-02-27)

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9936.description: To amend title 39, United States Code, to limit bonuses to the Postmaster General, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9936.aiSummary: The bill would limit bonuses and other performance pay for the Postmaster General if the Postal Service lost money, missed nationwide service goals, got a serious audit finding, or did not file a required report to Congress. US-119-HR9914.title: Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9914.description: To establish the applicability of antitrust laws to the sharing of artificial intelligence frontier model risks, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9914.aiSummary: The bill would let non-federal groups share information or help each other on certain AI security risks without breaking antitrust laws, if they act in good faith for that purpose. It would also let them agree to delay or limit some AI release, use, development, training, testing, or evaluation if they first give written notice to the Justice Department’s antitrust chief. The bill would let the Attorney General ask a court to stop conduct that still breaks antitrust laws or could raise those AI security risks.

US-119-HR9815.title: Federal Bureau of Prisons Voting Assistance Act of 2026
US-119-HR9815.summary:
Federal Bureau of Prisons Voting Assistance Act of 2026

This bill requires the Bureau of Prisons (BOP) to provide information about voting to inmates from jurisdictions that allow inmates to vote while in custody.

Specifically, before a federal, state, or local election, the BOP must send voting information to inmates, such as how to register to vote and how to request an absentee ballot. The BOP must send additional voting information to the reentry affairs coordinator at each federal correctional facility. The information must be provided in English and Spanish.

It would also have to give this information in English and Spanish to reentry staff at each federal prison.
